title: Prefix-fenced KV retirement: correctness guarantees under continuous batching and GPU memory compaction
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: As continuous batching increases throughput, our KV cache experiences more concurrent accesses with variable prefix locality. Traditional LRU/TTL eviction strategies cause visible regressions: prefix thrashing, increased tail latency from cache-miss storms, and GPU memory fragmentation that prevents large slab allocations. This ticket designs and implements a prefix-fenced retirement protocol for KV entries that provides provable safety and liveness guarantees when combined with batching and GPU compact/reclaim flows.

Goal: Introduce a lightweight epoch-and-fence mechanism that: (1) scopes eviction decisions to prefix cohorts, (2) prevents premature reclamation while in-flight batches may reference entries, (3) enables deterministic post-eviction invalidation across distributed GPU shards, and (4) cooperates with our slab compaction to minimize fragmentation. The protocol must be auditable, testable under fuzzed batching workloads, and support gradual rollout with a canary that can fall back to current LRU+TTL policy.

High-level approach:
- Each prefix cohort gets a small epoch counter and a per-entry fence token stamped on allocation.
- Batches snapshot the current epoch for every prefix they touch; eviction requires epoch advancement and a quorum of fence expirations.
- We leverage a lease-style pinning for short-lived in-flight KV references (batch pin tokens) to ensure entries cannot be reclaimed until all in-flight pins are released. Pins are cheap (8 bytes) and aggregated per-batch to avoid per-token RPC pressure.
- TTL remains an advisory score combined with LRU rank; entries are retired only when both TTL and fence/epoch conditions allow.
- On GPU reclaim, we use a two-phase compaction: logical retirement (entry marked retired but memory retained) then physical free after compaction fence to avoid fragmentation windows under active batching.

Correctness guarantees: Safety: no batch can observe an entry after it is logically retired and memory reclaimed. Liveness: under steady-state request patterns and bounded batch durations, retirement will complete within bounded timeouts (configurable). Determinism: with deterministic epoch advancement policy and globally ordered fence revocations per prefix, retirement ordering is reproducible in tests.

Why this is different: Previous tickets focused on eviction heuristics (LRU/TTL hybrids) or lease anchoring separately. This work ties prefix locality, batching snapshotting, and GPU compaction into a single retirement protocol with explicit fences and test harnesses that can prove invariants under concurrency and simulated GPU fragmentation.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by runtime and infra leads (link to doc in links)
Unit + integration tests that simulate concurrent batches (including fuzzed network delays) and assert no use-after-free for KV entries

Performance bench: end-to-end tail latency (p99 generation latency) does not regress more than 3% on 95th percentile workload vs baseline; cache hit-rate improves or is neutral for prefix-heavy traces
Memory fragmentation metric (holes_per_gpu_slab) reduced by >= 20% in compaction-enabled runs
Canary rollout plan with automated rollback if miss storm or latency spike > 15%
Production observability added: per-prefix epoch, retired_count, pinned_count, reclamation_latency metrics
tasks: Write detailed design doc (include state diagrams and pseudocode for epoch+fence flows)
Implement batch pinning API and fast path (C++ runtime) with minimal allocation overhead
Add epoch counters and fence tokens to KV metadata layout; ensure ABI compatibility with on-disk checkpoints
Implement two-phase reclaim: logical retire + compaction fence + physical free in GPU allocator
Create deterministic simulator to replay batches + evictions and assert invariants
Integrate metrics and console dashboards for observability (epochs, pins, reclamation latency, fragmentation)
End-to-end benchmark on scale-6 cluster and compare vs current LRU+TTL baseline
Canary rollout: implement flag gating and gradual traffic ramp for runtime-2.3
Document migration steps for Dedicated/Private deployments and KMS keys for auditability
comments: 2026-02-12: Design kickoff with runtime and infra. Agreed to avoid global GC pauses; prefer per-prefix epochs. Action: Aisha to draft doc.

2026-02-18: Architecture review. Concern from SRE about metric cardinality from per-prefix epochs — agreed to sample long-tail prefixes and aggregate metrics for dashboard. Action: Liam to add aggregation layer.
2026-02-25: Prototype batch pin tokens landed in feature-branch (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7268). Initial microbench shows +1% CPU and negligible memory overhead.

2026-03-03: Simulator results: under synthetic prefix-thrash workload, no use-after-free observed across 10k runs; some slow retire cases correlated with long-lived batches (>5s) — added configurable pin timeout and forced-advance policy.
2026-03-08: Perf run on scale-6 cluster: p99 latency improved 4% for prefix-heavy traces, fragmentation reduced ~24% after compaction pass. Need to validate on real traffic canary.
2026-03-11: Security review requested (security_review_required=true). Security raised audit logging requirements for fence revocations; added to tasks.
